4. In `_neighbor_mask`, `rows = max(1, min(size, (1 << 21)//max(1, size*8)))` → for size=4096: 2097152/32768 = 64 rows per chunk → the chunk temps are 64×4096 float64 = 2MB ✓.

5. The BFS: `row_bits[node]` — `node` comes from `pending` bits which are core uids ✓ (pending starts as the core bitmask and only clears bits) ✓ and row_bits has entries for all core uids ✓.

6. `pending = int.from_bytes(np.packbits(core, bitorder='little').tobytes(), 'little')` — packbits on a bool array of length `size` → ceil(size/8) bytes ✓; bit i = core[i] ✓ with bitorder='little' meaning the first element is the LSB of the first byte ✓.    Careful: `np.packbits(core, bitorder='little')` pads the last byte with zeros ✓.

7. `packed_rows = np.packbits(rows, axis=1, bitorder='little')` → for each row, bit j = rows[i,j] ✓. Then `int.from_bytes(packed_rows[i].tobytes(), 'little')` ✓ gives bit j = neighbor j (core only) ✓.

   Note: `adjacent` is (chunk, size) uint8 → np.where broadcasts identity_of (size,) ✓.
